chunks.text: Ever notice stores play slow, calm music? It's not just to be nice.
Music can change how fast you walk.
In a famous study, one supermarket switched between slow and fast music for nine weeks.
With slow music, shoppers walked slower. And in that store, sales went up about thirty-eight percent.
Fast music did the opposite. It moved people along.
Restaurants too. In another study, slow music kept diners at their tables about ten minutes longer. And they bought more drinks.
It gets weirder. One store played French accordion music, and French wine outsold German wine.
Then it played German music, and German wine sold more. Most shoppers didn't think the music mattered.
So Tony tried slow jazz. But careful: later studies found it depends on the song.
And it was one store, so results can vary.
Next time: why the medium popcorn is a trap. That's part five.
Until then, if the music is slow, check your pace, and your cart.
